v1.feedback: The thumbnail reveals the strings have collapsed into a flat, ground-hugging mesh rather than reading as hanging catenaries — the gravity constant (0.008) plus 500 pre-steps has dragged everything to the bottom of frame, producing a topographic particle carpet instead of the Gonzalez-Torres light-string drape the concept promises. The form needs vertical presence: either pin anchor points higher (y=3+), reduce gravity, or cut pre-steps to ~200 so the strings still read as suspended curves at first render. The Kusama dot-rain surprise system — the entire creative swerve of this piece — is invisible in the thumbnail, suggesting either the capture missed the 14s window or the dots are too small/dim against the already-dense string particles; give the rain dots a distinct size bump (3-4x point size) and a cooler tint (bone/chalk vs the amber strings) so they register as a separate visual event.

v2.feedback: The warm amber-on-ink palette is excellent and the two-phase Gonzalez-Torres-to-Kusama concept is genuinely poetic, but the thumbnail reads as a flat particle terrain rather than suspended catenaries — the catenary drape needs stronger vertical hang with visible anchor points at top-of-frame so the 'light string' silhouette is recognizable in under 2 seconds. Raise the anchor pins to y≈7+ and increase gravity so the sag is unmistakable, and consider rendering the strings as thin Line2 traces (you already import LineMaterial) with particles as secondary glow, so the string identity survives before the dot-rain phase arrives. The dot-rain phase should use larger, fewer spheres (radius 0.15+, N≤200) to read as Kusama's obsessive polka-dot scale rather than more small particles blending into the existing field.
